config.name: photonic_focus_heatmaps
config.description: Grayscale print tuning for the focusing experiments: each item is one experiment with its Initial and Final camera heatmaps, printed in several grayscale variations per round, scanned by the user and judged by the agents to pick a better gamma. Only gamma is tuned, in all three rounds.

page.description: Each page shows items_per_page items, each printed in variations_per_item variations, so one page has items_per_page x variations_per_item tiles.

panels.description: The figures inside one item. For this project an item has 2 heatmap panels: the Initial and the Final camera image.

limits.description: The value limits that map data to gray are computed once from all panels of an item together and stay fixed for the whole calibration session, so the panels of an item stay comparable and only gamma changes between rounds.

gamma.description: Tone curve applied to the normalized data; values below 1 brighten the low values, above 1 darken them. Test values are spaced on a log scale.

gray_levels.description: The printed gray for the lowest (dark) and highest (light) data values, where 0 means black and 1 means white. Not tuned: always printed with the defaults, dark 0.0 and light 1.0.

steps.description: Number of discrete gray bands. 0 means smooth (no banding). Not tuned: always printed with the default 0 (smooth).

invert.description: If true, high data values print dark instead of light. Not tuned; set by hand if needed.

variation_rules.description: Each item's variations include reference_count copies of the best settings so far; the other variations change only the parameter of the current round. A shared parameter gets the same test values in every item.

references.description: Printed on every page for reading the scan: gray_patches patches evenly spaced from 0 to 1, paper_refs blank paper areas, one full black patch, and markers corner markers for aligning the scan, with a page code that identifies the page and round.

scan.description: Requirements for the scanned page the user returns.

experiment_dbff339b85ce42699275093e1e0ba.note: The previews look very dark, especially in both Initial and Final. This low gamma starts a log-spaced sweep toward brighter low and mid intensities.
A log-spaced lower-gamma test to assess whether brightening reveals useful detail in both panels without losing their intensity structure.
A central, log-spaced brightening test for the dark-looking Initial and Final previews.
A milder brightening test that helps compare the dark previews against less aggressive tone adjustment.
An upper log-spaced comparison point to check whether preserving darker tones offers better separation than brightening.

experiment_0bf9ddf950094096a83ef6e54da60.note: Both previews appear very dark. This low gamma begins a log-spaced sweep toward revealing low- and mid-intensity detail.
A log-spaced lower-gamma test to see whether moderate brightening improves readability in both Initial and Final.
A central brightening test for the predominantly dark-looking previews.
A milder brightening comparison that may reveal detail while retaining separation between intensity levels.
An upper log-spaced comparison point to test whether retaining darker tones is preferable to brightening.

experiment_d4c01d44524c4b6d8fdf4d3f2d780.note: The previews show a broad range of dark through bright texture. This lower end tests whether brightening improves low-intensity detail in both panels.
A log-spaced brightening test to compare low-intensity visibility against the currently varied appearance.
A near-reference comparison point within the log-spaced sweep, allowing a modest brightening to be assessed.
A log-spaced darkening test to assess whether bright regions and intermediate levels become easier to distinguish.
The upper sweep point tests stronger darkening as a comparison for preserving detail among the brighter parts of Initial and Final.

experiment_e309e0568d494bce9e80704fbc901.note: The previews contain substantial visible texture across a broad range. This lower log-spaced point tests whether further brightening benefits darker detail in both panels.
A moderate brightening test to compare low-intensity readability while retaining visible midtone structure.
A near-reference comparison point for evaluating a small shift toward darker tones in Initial and Final.
A log-spaced darkening test to assess separation and detail in the relatively bright, textured previews.
The upper sweep point tests stronger darkening as a comparison for retaining detail in brighter regions without relying on brightness alone.
